utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. Good morning. As promised yesterday, we have the copies of the statement of Mr. Abullah Salihu and, pursuant to Rule 92 bis, we would now offer that into admission, please, into evidence. And I would again ask the Honourable Judges and the other parties to please make note of the correction by the witness yesterday on the second page where it says "200.000 people." It should say "20.000."

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be marked Prosecutor's Exhibit 142.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Before I begin, I'd like to make an objection and say that we didn't get a summary yesterday that was provided for this witness yesterday, but let me move on to my questions.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: Cross-examined by Mr. Milosevic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In your statement, you say that you finished your primary school in Cirez; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ABDULLAH SALIHU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All eight years of schooling there?

utterances.speaker: ABDULLAH SALIHU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I finished the eight years school in Cirez, the high school in another place, and the university in Prishtina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you study in Pristina?

utterances.speaker: ABDULLAH SALIHU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nothing. I didn't study anything. I did only the high school, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A moment ago I understood when you said you attended the university of Pristina that you actually did. Were you at the university or not?

utterances.speaker: ABDULLAH SALIHU [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, no. I did -- I did the primary school in Cirez, the high school in Prishtina. It is called Medresa. That is the high school.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that a religious school?

utterances.speaker: ABDULLAH SALIHU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: May we then conclude that you know the village of Cirez very well and its inhabitants too?

utterances.speaker: ABDULLAH SALIHU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you do between 1986 until September 1998?

utterances.speaker: ABDULLAH SALIHU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Until then, I worked in the construction field. I did a course on construction, and I worked as a construction worker then. Until four years ago, I worked as imam in Baks village. As a Muslim priest.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. I understand. So you worked in the field of construction, and you also worked as a hodza, a Muslim priest, at the same time; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ABDULLAH SALIHU [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time, I did not work as hoxha, but I did a construction course and worked as a construction worker until four years ago.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you worked in the village of Baks as a hodza. Did you work as a hodza anywhere else, apart from the village of Baks?

utterances.speaker: ABDULLAH SALIHU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I worked also in Jashanica village, '74/'75.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Also as a hodza; right?

utterances.speaker: ABDULLAH SALIHU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how long did you work as hodza in the village of Baks? From when until when?

utterances.speaker: ABDULLAH SALIHU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I worked as hoxha for 25 years in the month of Ramadan. It's only one month a year. Now I work as imam, because now we have built a mosque in the Baks village, and this is where I work now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your statement, you say that 80 per cent of the population left the village of Baks and that only a few people remained - and they were men - to look after the cattle; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ABDULLAH SALIHU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many men stayed on?

utterances.speaker: ABDULLAH SALIHU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Several men. I couldn't say how many exactly, but during the first offensive in September of 1998, the Serb rebellion, that is the onslaught which came from Gllogoc-Skenderaj, has driven the population out to Cicavica mountain where over 20.000 people were gathered in those places. The Baks village was totally burnt, or if not exactly 100 per cent, 90 per cent of the houses were burnt. So that offensive ended, which lasted for two days. After that, we received some aid from the OSCE. I don't --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone. Microphone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Salihu, I'm going to interrupt you. If you just listen to the questions and just answer them, we'll get on more quickly.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As we were saying, how many men stayed on in the village when, as you say, the population left the village? Men to tend to the livestock, that is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: He said that he couldn't say exactly. Can you give us a rough idea, Mr. Salihu?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] About 20, 30, because there was no place where the population could go to. I told you, 90 per cent of the houses were burned down.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. I'm asking you how many remained in the village, because you said that the men stayed on to tend to the livestock.

utterances.speaker: ABDULLAH SALIHU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I'm saying 20, 30 men.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Very well. Now, those men, were they armed?

utterances.speaker: ABDULLAH SALIHU [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they were not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, if they weren't armed, how can you talk about an attack on the village?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: What does that question mean? Just a moment. Let's see if we can understand the question. What does the question mean, Mr. Milosevic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, in the village, there were 20 to 30 people who were not armed, and the witness claims that an attack was launched on the village which was empty except for a few unarmed people.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ABDULLAH SALIHU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told you the offensive was launched in October 1998, and they burned all the houses. The population had no place where to go. Therefore, only 20, 30 people could stay, could put their heads somewhere, could find some shelter. And these people were unarmed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please. You said that 80 per cent of the villagers had left the village of Baks and that the people -- some people stayed on to tend to the livestock, and then you said that an offensive followed. Is that right? Is that what you said?

utterances.speaker: ABDULLAH SALIHU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I'm talking about the offensive of 1998. Then after that, the houses were burned down. I don't know what you don't understand here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I don't want anything. I'm just asking you in connection with your statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: This is at complete cross-purposes. Now, I suggest you move on to another question.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say that between 180 and 190 people were killed in the area. On the basis of what do you base this assertion?

utterances.speaker: ABDULLAH SALIHU [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the Cicavica offensive. It is true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you're talking about the fighting that went on at Cicavica; right?

utterances.speaker: ABDULLAH SALIHU [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was no fighting. There was only an offensive mounted on it by the Serb army. It was shelling from a distance of 10, 15 kilometres, so that when we returned there, there was no house standing almost. As I said, it came from Gllogoc-Skenderaj. They had shelled Cicavica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Salihu, let's clear something up. You said a moment ago an offensive at Mount Cicavica; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ABDULLAH SALIHU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, do you know that on the Cicavica mountain there were strong forces of the KLA? Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: ABDULLAH SALIHU [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is not true that there were KLA forces in the Cicavica mountain at that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Then we can move on because, according to you, there were no forces of the KLA on Cicavica. Now, who were your sources of information with respect to what you say and what you say went on on Mount Cicavica?

utterances.speaker: ABDULLAH SALIHU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was one of those who fled with my family, with my neighbours, with my nephews and nieces. We all together went there to that place. I experienced that myself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So this confirms once again, unless I'm mistaken, that you're a very well-informed man about all the events that were taking place. Can we draw that conclusion?

utterances.speaker: ABDULLAH SALIHU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am well-informed about what I have stated in my statement, because I went through it myself, and I am certain of what I'm saying.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Help us about this: The figure of 180 to 190 people killed at this time, what is that based on? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Because at least 30, 40 people I helped myself to bury with my own hands.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May we proceed?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you happen to know, then, that the KLA terrorists were especially dangerous in their attacks day and night, especially in the village of Cirez? Do you know about that?

utterances.speaker: ABDULLAH SALIHU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about the terrorists. I know the KLA was not dangerous. I know that the KLA defended the people as much as they could and were capable of.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. That is your description of the character of their activities. Now, I'm asking you whether you know about that particular activity of theirs.

utterances.speaker: ABDULLAH SALIHU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said the KLA defended the people, stood up for the people.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Well, help us with this: In the period we're dealing with, which is the autumn of 1998, September and October, were the KLA in Cirez or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There -- there was in Cirez, in Pelez, but the KLA, and I'm sure of what I'm saying, that the KLA was not a terrorist organisation. It defended the people. That was our only support.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. I'm not asking you actually about the character or in your opinion what their activities were like, but I asked you whether they were there, and you said yes. Now, does the name Muj Krasniqi Kapuci mean anything to you? Do you know the name?

utterances.speaker: ABDULLAH SALIHU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've heard about him, but I don't know him personally.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. If you've heard of him, even if you don't know him personally, do you know that, in the area, he killed policemen, for example? Do you know about that?

utterances.speaker: ABDULLAH SALIHU [Resumed]
utterances.text: This I don't know. That was probably a secret of the KLA.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... move on. And do you know who Ramush Haradinaj is?

utterances.speaker: ABDULLAH SALIHU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know. He is from Gjakove, and I am from Drenica. It's about 70 to 80 kilometres away. And I have heard his voice on television.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know that this man, Muj Krasniqi Kapuci, whom you've heard of, together with Ramush Haradinaj, was active in the area, in that region, in the district, and that they perpetrated a series of actions in which many people were killed or kidnapped? Do you know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: ABDULLAH SALIHU [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't. I don't have any information on this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you perhaps see a book of his, a dialogue, in fact --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: He has no information on this. Now, let's move on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. Let's stick to what he does have information about.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said in Cirez, in the surrounding villages, that the KLA was there. Now, what were they doing in concrete terms there? What were they doing specifically?

utterances.speaker: ABDULLAH SALIHU [Resumed]
utterances.text: The people were relying on them. And this was the only support we had. We didn't have any protection but the KLA.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please. I'm asking you what they did. I'm asking you what they did physically speaking.

utterances.speaker: ABDULLAH SALIHU [Resumed]
utterances.text: And I'm telling you: They were defending the people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Describe how they were defending the people, then.

utterances.speaker: ABDULLAH SALIHU [Resumed]
utterances.text: If there was any need. But there wasn't even any -- there wasn't even any opportunity, because the shelling was from a distance. They didn't even have a chance to defend us. Because the KLA was not situated inside the village. It was always five, six kilometres away, therefore, it did not have any real link with the civilian population.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. A moment ago, you said that in Cirez, and you mentioned another village which is in the transcript here but I can't remember its name just now, that the KLA was there. Now you say that they were outside the village. Were they in the village or were they outside the village?

utterances.speaker: ABDULLAH SALIHU [Resumed]
utterances.text: The KLA was always at a distance from people, and it didn't have contact with people. It was five or six kilometres away. It kept at a distance from the civilians.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. That's a little different from what you said a moment ago. Now, in your statement, you say that nobody from your village was killed; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ABDULLAH SALIHU [Resumed]
utterances.text: What? I didn't understand the question. At that time, nobody was killed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where do you get these 180 and 190 people who were allegedly killed that you referred to?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: He's already answered that. He said he buried 40 of them himself.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There were at least 40 villagers at that time in the offensive, villagers who had gathered in Cirez from Klina to Gllogoc. All the villages from Cicavica -- all the villages roundabout had gathered on Cicavica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Salihu, those whom you buried, did you bury as part of your duties as imam?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. There were groups of villagers, and we buried the bodies together.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You buried KLA members who had been killed at Cicavica. Is that right or not?

utterances.speaker: ABDULLAH SALIHU [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not true. I buried civilians and also Les Gradica [as interpreted], a doctor, who was one of the people massacred at Cicavica and mutilated. He had a hand cut off. I didn't bury any of the soldiers of the KLA because none were killed. There were only civilians.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So there were no KLA soldiers who had died?

utterances.speaker: ABDULLAH SALIHU [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there weren't any killed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So in all those villages, the KLA was there, there was an offensive, but none of the KLA members were killed. So the offensive was not against the KLA, it was against the civilians. Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: ABDULLAH SALIHU [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in which places were these people killed?

utterances.speaker: ABDULLAH SALIHU [Resumed]
utterances.text: These people were killed in the village of Grabofc and also in Dubofc. Cicavica is about 13 kilometres long, and this was the area where this happened.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see it? Did you see them being killed?

utterances.speaker: ABDULLAH SALIHU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told you that I buried them. I couldn't see them all being killed. This would have been impossible. I might have seen three or four, but I saw one person from Kozhnice when a shell hit a tree, and a father and son were killed when the tree fell on them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that's what you saw with your own eyes: You saw those two people killed when a tree fell on top of them. Is that it?

utterances.speaker: ABDULLAH SALIHU [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the matter of the shell cutting the tree, and it wasn't the matter of the tree. It was a father and a son. The father got killed and the son is still alive.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand. So that's what you saw personally yourself.

utterances.speaker: ABDULLAH SALIHU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A moment ago, you said that the KLA did not have occasion to defend the people, because our forces were shooting from a distance; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ABDULLAH SALIHU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course. The shelling was from 10, 15 kilometres away. Gllogoc and Skenderaj.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So are you saying that the members of the KLA didn't shoot at all because they didn't have anybody to shoot at? Is that it?

utterances.speaker: ABDULLAH SALIHU [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was no KLA there. Please, Mr. Milosevic, don't mix up my statement. The KLA was to defend the people. I -- there was no KLA there. I told you. There were only civilians, and the shelling was aimed at Cicavica, and they even dug holes on the ground. Everything was destroyed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Did the KLA at this period, as far as you could see, did they fire any shots? Did you see any firing from the KLA?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. Fire was not opened.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That means that they had no one to shoot at, because our forces were operating from a distance. Is that what you said? Is that your explanation?

utterances.speaker: ABDULLAH SALIHU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I -- I'm saying that we -- all these people were gathered on the mountains of Cicavica, and they came from -- with tanks towards all the people gathered there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A little while ago, you mentioned trenches that they had dug. Who was it that had dug the trenches?

utterances.speaker: ABDULLAH SALIHU [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not true that this is what I said. I said that after the offensive, two days later, we buried people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I asked you about the trenches that you referred to a short while ago. Who had dug these trenches?

utterances.speaker: ABDULLAH SALIHU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't say that. There were no trenches. I replied that after the offensive, we buried people. We were not able to leave them just lying on the ground. And I mentioned one man whom I saw myself mutilated, Dr. Lesi [phoen] from Gradica. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Salihu, do you know of any occasion in that period when there was any fight between the KLA and the Serb forces; any occasion in which the KLA and the Serb forces were engaged in a fight?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. In that period, there was not. In that period, there was a KLA, but they were unable to fight. And after the offensive, they were shattered. No, there was no -- there were no clashes at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Milosevic, you've been cross-examining for half an hour. We have not got beyond the first page of his statement, the witness's statement. As you know, it contains the most serious allegations of mistreatment. He was present at an execution. All of that he describes. If you're going to challenge that, you should do so in the next half hour rather than dealing with these preliminary matters.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I fully challenge that, because this is certainly not true. However, I do not expect the witness to say that this is not true, because the witnesses who come here, some of them, say such untruths that somebody probably had to instruct them to behave that way. You don't really think that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: You don't -- you don't make a speech now. If you're going to challenge that this witness is telling untruths, then you must put it to him so he's got a chance to answer. And if you're making suggestions about instructions of how witnesses should give evidence, then you must put them to the witnesses so they can answer. It's no good making wild allegations to us.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. All right. A short while ago, the witness said that after the offensive, the KLA had been broken.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ABDULLAH SALIHU [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And before that, you said that in that -- that the KLA did not even participate in that offensive. How could it be shattered in an offensive in which it did not even participate?

utterances.speaker: ABDULLAH SALIHU [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is possible because of the shelling by the Serbian army. The KLA had no -- was not able to confront this. The KLA kept up its morale and tried to strengthen itself after the offensive. I have never been a member of the KLA myself, but I regret it now that I wasn't a member. And I kindly ask you to read my statement to see that if I had a gun myself --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I didn't ask you that, whether you were sorry that you were not a member of the KLA. I didn't ask you that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: One at a time. Now, what's the next question?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know, do you know that in 1998 there were very intensive actions launched by the KLA terrorists against the police and against other citizens precisely in your area; Selimi Sulltan, Zoltarasahi [phoen] Jashari from Donji Prekazi, Sabit Geci from Lausa? They figured the most prominently. As a matter of fact, he was wounded and he found shelter in Baks, in your village. Do you know them and do you know about these events in view of the role of your village in that? Do you know about that?

utterances.speaker: ABDULLAH SALIHU [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is not true that Shabit Geci came to Baks village. That is untrue. And he was not injured in Baks village. And I have not heard that Sulltan Selimi, as you call him, has attacked anyone. Or Jashari, I didn't get well the name you mentioned; I have not heard of them attacking the police. I have no information about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. You don't know anything about this.

utterances.speaker: ABDULLAH SALIHU [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's not waste any time since you don't know anything about this. And do you remember, for example, as far as back as 1994 --

utterances.speaker: ABDULLAH SALIHU [Resumed]
utterances.text: You should ask me about what I know and what I have testified.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm asking you because you're a very informed person. You worked as a hodza, and you know everybody in the area. As far as back as 1994, do you know Shefqet Dibrani, a forest keeper who was maltreated and afterwards killed by the KLA? Have you heard of him?

utterances.speaker: ABDULLAH SALIHU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Shefqet Dibrani was killed by your offspring, not by the KLA. He was killed in Skenderaj. And you know very well who killed him, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So you do know of the killing of Shefqet Dibrani, a forestkeeper employed by the state.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: He's given his answer. Don't -- there's no need to go on. Yes, let's move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you remember when these same terrorists maltreated Halim Halil and his father Hasan, a farmer from Cirez? Do you know about that?

utterances.speaker: ABDULLAH SALIHU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you tell me how many young men the KLA recruited in the village of Baks and Cirez?

utterances.speaker: ABDULLAH SALIHU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many were recruited?

utterances.speaker: ABDULLAH SALIHU [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Baks, there were seven, and four in Cirez, as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Only those 11?

utterances.speaker: ABDULLAH SALIHU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those are the ones I know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. They were recruited forcibly by the KLA; is that right or is that not right?

utterances.speaker: ABDULLAH SALIHU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not forcibly. As I said, I would have wished to have been a member of the KLA, looking back today, but I didn't have that luck.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. But I'm not asking you about that. You claim that they were not forcibly recruited. And now, is it correct that as a hodza -- as a hodza, you convoyed messages from Allah about a jihad, a holy war, to these same soldiers? Is that right or is that not right?

utterances.speaker: ABDULLAH SALIHU [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is it true -- is it true that in 1994, among the hodzas an agreement was reached to say to the faithful that they can take false oaths before the authorities and that that is the agreement that was reached among the hodzas? Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ABDULLAH SALIHU [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not true. I have -- I can say that what is in my statement is absolutely true, everything that I said. But Mr. Milosevic is not asking me about my statement, because when I was taken prisoner --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Just try and answer the questions, if you would.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. In your statement, do you not know actually about a single element about this, that the hodzas agreed that the faithful can take false oaths? You don't know nothing about that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: He said it's not true, so there's no point arguing about it.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. In your statement, you do not explain at all the period between September 1998 to March 1999. Where were you in that period and what did you do?

utterances.speaker: ABDULLAH SALIHU [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said before, 20 and 25 of us went back to the village with the USA and I was there in my village, and we had some tents and improvised shelters in my village, and that's where we were up to 29th, 30th April, when the second offensive came, I can say one of the toughest offensives that ever took place in Kosova in what is known as Fusha e Molles.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So you were in the village all that time. All right. But in the statement, you say that you were arrested in the forest on the 29th of April, between Baks, Vrbovac, and Cirez, in that triangle.

utterances.speaker: ABDULLAH SALIHU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say that 11 persons were arrested with you and that all of them were your relatives. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ABDULLAH SALIHU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If they are your relatives, how come you don't know the three -- three -- the names of three of them?

utterances.speaker: ABDULLAH SALIHU [Resumed]
utterances.text: These names were not mentioned because they were not from my village. So I didn't mention the names. I only mentioned the names of the people from my village. Because on that day when we were captured in Fusha e Molles, which is surrounded by the villages of Baks, Cirez, Trstenik, Glogar, Studica, Gllogofc, this place is known as Fusha e Molles, and on that day --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Don't go on for a minute. Yes, Mr. Milosevic, the next question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you were arrested in the village or were you arrested in the forest? You said that you were arrested in the forest, and now you said that you were arrested in the village. So where were you arrested; in the forest or in the village?

utterances.speaker: ABDULLAH SALIHU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't say in the village but in the place called Fusha e Molles. We had -- all those villages that I mentioned, people had been expelled from them. And we were gathered - men, women, children, the elderly, young people - on Fusha e Molles.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. You've answered my question. When you were arrested, where did they take you?

utterances.speaker: ABDULLAH SALIHU [Resumed]
utterances.text: They took us to the mosque at the village of Cirez, which is now being demolished.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. If you were arrested and if you were taken to the mosque in the village of Cirez, how did you know what was happening on the 29th of April when you were arrested? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I don't follow that question. What do you mean?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The question is the following: If he was arrested and taken to the mosque, how could he know what was happening on that day when he was not there?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Which passage in the statement are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can say that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Let's see what the question is.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can see the paragraph now. He has two statements here. He speaks about events --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Is this the passage you have in mind: "On Friday, the 29th of April, a new, very big Serb offensive started against the entire area. The offensive lasted for three days. Area after area was attacked day by day." Now, the question is: If you were in the mosque, how did you know what was going on elsewhere?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When they captured us that day, it was 29th of April, and they took us to the mosque, and that night, we stayed in the mosque. On the next day, we saw them attacking again the place where we had been captured. And in the morning, about three jeeps came, three or four, belonging to the Serbian military, and they took out 176 people who had been in the mosque, and they took us to Gllogoc. Before taking us to Gllogoc, in the place known as Shavari, three trucks came, and although there were people still remaining at the mosque, about 32 people were taken off the trucks at Shavari, and I saw with my own eyes, I saw them being shot.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: That's what you yourself saw and experienced.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I was present myself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Is there anything else or any other knowledge which you have? You say, "The offensive lasted for three days," and, "Area after area was attacked day by day." Now, what is that based on?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is what I heard, going to Shavarina. And after I went to Gllogoc, they kept us in the cinema, and then they brought another group from there to Gllogoc, and then they told us that they were still fighting, the offensive was still continuing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was fighting? Well, thank you that my turn has finally come. So who was fighting?

utterances.speaker: ABDULLAH SALIHU [Resumed]
utterances.text: It wasn't fighting, it was civilians. A child of nine was killed, a five-month-old child was killed. Elderly people were killed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please. You said only a minute ago, "They were still fighting." "They were still fighting," and then when I ask you who, and then you say there was no fighting. So were they fighting or were they not fighting? Yes or no. Let's not waste any time.

utterances.speaker: ABDULLAH SALIHU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said it was not fighting, it was fighting against civilians. I said that we were there with our members of our families.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. All right. I know about that explanation. According to that explanation, the KLA was not fighting at all. Please. You say that they took you to --

utterances.speaker: ABDULLAH SALIHU [Resumed]
utterances.text: It fought when the need arose.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So then you claim that there was no need for them to struggle --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreters note that it is impossible to interpret two speakers at a time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Salihu, would you wait, please, until the interpretation is finished. Otherwise, there is difficulty for the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, there is a problem. He knows Serbian and he wants to answer straightaway. He can't wait for all this stage management.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say that they took you to some field, that they beat you in the process and that they had the intention -- you claim that they had the intention to kill you by a tank, by trampling over you with a tank. And then since NATO aeroplanes were flying above, they did not start the tank. They fled from NATO aircraft. That is to say that you were free then, because our soldiers had fled from you. Is that right or is that not right? You say that the Serb soldiers fled to the woods, including --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Let him answer what's being put.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When they captured us, we were 65 people. They laid us out on the ground. They beat us. And one of the leaders of the military gave the order to push us back.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please. That was not my question.

utterances.speaker: ABDULLAH SALIHU [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is in my statement, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Let him explain. Now, what happened? What happened when the aircraft came?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He ordered us -- the tank to trample over us, our bodies, but at that moment, thanks to God and NATO, the tank changed its direction and we were safe. Then they took us to the mosque.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that the soldiers fled into the woods. You stayed in that meadow by yourselves.

utterances.speaker: ABDULLAH SALIHU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't mention that. The army, soldiers were around us. They were guarding us with their guns, automatic. And then they took us to the mosque.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please. Let us clear this up. They wanted to kill you with a tank, and since they did not kill you with a tank, they fled into the woods and then you were free. Does that mean that they returned yet again and arrested you again?

utterances.speaker: ABDULLAH SALIHU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, don't mix up my statement, please. I said that the tank changed its direction, but army was there. It was very close to us; maybe three, four metres away.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Salihu, in fairness to what the accused is putting, let me read out what it says in your statement. "The man in charge for the paramilitary unit ordered the driver of a tank to start the engine and run over us. We were in two lines, and the tank manoeuvred in direction to us. At the same time, NATO aeroplanes came and were circled over the area. All the Serb forces ran away into the woods, including the driver of the tank. The NATO aeroplanes stayed in the air for ten minutes. When the planes left, we were ordered to march in the direction of Cirez. The tank left in the direction of Studica. We had to march with our hands behind our heads." Now, the question was: How was it, if the Serb forces ran into the woods, that you came to be ordered to march in the direction of Cirez?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They only went away, let's say three metres or five metres, not more. They wanted to hide the tank from NATO planes, but the army troops were there, were very close to us. We were prisoners at that moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that in the morning?

utterances.speaker: ABDULLAH SALIHU [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was about 1.00, 2.00; midday.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Around noon then, midday. In broad daylight Serbian tanks are moving and NATO aircraft are flying, and they did not manage to notice Serb tanks that were moving. Are you trying to say that?

utterances.speaker: ABDULLAH SALIHU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I don't know whether the NATO planes saw the tanks or not. This I can't say. I know only this: Thanks to NATO, we managed to escape.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Well, obviously they couldn't see him. And you claim that they could not see a tank in broad daylight, at midday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: It's not a matter for him. He's given his evidence. There's nothing more he can say.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know what military experts would say about this particular statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From that place to the place of Shavarina, how long did that journey of yours take?

utterances.speaker: ABDULLAH SALIHU [Resumed]
utterances.text: From there, it is about five kilometres where the mosque of Cirez is situated. This is where they took us. We spent the night there. The mosque was destroyed. It was burned. Only the walls were still standing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. That's not what I'm asking you. As we have to save time, let me ask you this: Did you travel in trucks or on foot?

utterances.speaker: ABDULLAH SALIHU [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... telling you how they went there. From Fusha e Molles to the mosque, we walked on foot. From the mosque to Shavarina, we went there by trucks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Afterwards?

utterances.speaker: ABDULLAH SALIHU [Resumed]
utterances.text: From Shavarina, again by trucks to Gllogoc.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now we've come to the question that I asked you to begin with and I didn't get an answer to. Shavarina and Glogovac, you went on your way in trucks; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ABDULLAH SALIHU [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did those trucks have tarpaulins?

utterances.speaker: ABDULLAH SALIHU [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So they were open trucks, were they?

utterances.speaker: ABDULLAH SALIHU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in addition to yourself, how many other people were in the truck?

utterances.speaker: ABDULLAH SALIHU [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were about 22 besides me. That is we were, altogether, 23 persons. And I think that the same can be said of other -- the other three trucks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how many trucks were there in all?

utterances.speaker: ABDULLAH SALIHU [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were three. When they first took us from Cirez to Shavarina in the first crowd, the first group. But there were still people left behind, at the mosque. One of the trucks, as I said, the people on that truck were executed. I think they were about 32 people. They shot them. I saw them being shot at with my own eyes. The second truck and the third truck, they went to Gllogoc. Then a jeep came from Gllogoc, they said something among themselves, and then from there, the two other trucks were sent to Gllogoc, to the cinema.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Time is limited so perhaps you could just keep the answers fairly short. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How far were the trucks spaced out, one away from the other?

utterances.speaker: ABDULLAH SALIHU [Resumed]
utterances.text: As the case is usually with trucks driving one behind another. I didn't have a metre to measure. They may be 10, 15 metres away from one another.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in which truck in line were you?

utterances.speaker: ABDULLAH SALIHU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was on the third truck.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you say that in every truck there were about 20 people and that all the trucks were open. Is that it?

utterances.speaker: ABDULLAH SALIHU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I say that there were from 20 to 30 people in every truck, and they were open, without any tarpaulin.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why did they use so many trucks if there were only 20 people in Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. each truck?

utterances.speaker: ABDULLAH SALIHU [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were 176 persons, sir. Some people were still left behind in the mosque. I told you. We were about 65 people who left.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm talking about the people in the trucks. Now, from which truck were these people taken down whom you claim were shot?

utterances.speaker: ABDULLAH SALIHU [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the first truck. They ordered them to get down, and they were lined up in three rows. Three Serb soldiers with mortars and automatic rifles shot them one by one. I saw them being shot at with my own eyes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Abdullah, you don't wish to say that they were shot by mortars. Surely they weren't shot that way. And from a truck where there were 20 to 30, surely they did just not take down 30-odd people. Do you realise what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: ABDULLAH SALIHU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I understand very well, but I think you don't understand me. I went through that myself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Just a moment. Did you say "mortars"? That was the way it was translated.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said mortar at the end. Yes, when they were shot, they threw also a mortar -- a hand grenade, actually. I haven't spoken about that yet. It is at the end of my statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, your time is now up. You can ask two or three more questions.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, after this, I don't know whether I need ask any more questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But can you tell me the names of the people who were executed? They were all people from your village.

utterances.speaker: ABDULLAH SALIHU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could tell you. Some of them I don't remember. There were three -- the first three who were killed, their bodies were burned. Now, Xhevat Osmani, Sejdi Osmani, Hysen Zaqiri, they were burned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, that's a new fact. Please. In your statement, you claim that people were killed with three --

utterances.speaker: ABDULLAH SALIHU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't mention them in my statement, but he asked me about the village. Thirty-eight people were killed in my village, but I didn't note these people in my statement, but he asked me about my village, and I'm giving details about how many were killed in my village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Out of 34 people killed from your village, how many of them were members of the KLA of those 38? Thirty-eight people killed, sorry.

utterances.speaker: ABDULLAH SALIHU [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were no members of the KLA. Five-year-old children, infants, elderly people of 80 or 90, how can they be members of the KLA?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Very well. I -- now with respect to the execution that you've been talking about, you claim in your statement -- let me refresh your memory -- you say that people were killed with three, four individual bullets. Is that right? Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: ABDULLAH SALIHU [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And a moment ago, you said that they were all killed from a machine-gun, a mortar, and so on and so forth, and now you've added that they were burnt too, that they burnt.

utterances.speaker: ABDULLAH SALIHU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would ask this gentleman -- I said they were killed by individual shots, not by a volley of shots. And after the execution was finished, they threw a grenade on top of them. This is what I saw with my own eyes. This is a hundred per cent true.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: That will conclude the examination. Mr. Kay, is there anything you want to ask?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Your Honour. Questioned by Mr. Kay:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Salihu, you told the Court that on the 29th of April, as a result of a Serb offensive, that was when you moved from your area; is that right? Just say yes or no.

utterances.speaker: ABDULLAH SALIHU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want to ask you about what happened the day before that, as in your statement you've told this account, that on Thursday, the 28th of April, NATO aeroplanes attacked Ferronikel factories in Gllogoc.

utterances.speaker: ABDULLAH SALIHU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, uh-huh. There were Serbs there and, for that reason, NATO attacked it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you in your village of Baks at that time?

utterances.speaker: ABDULLAH SALIHU [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I was at Fusha e Molles. It's nearby, about two or three kilometres away. Two or three kilometres away, Fusha e Molles, from Baks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you able to see NATO planes bombing the factories?

utterances.speaker: ABDULLAH SALIHU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We only saw the vapour in the air because we were in a kind of valley. And this was about seven or eight or nine kilometres away from us. Ferronikel is quite a distance away.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The Ferronikel factories, are they close to the centre of the town of Gllogoc, near the railway station?

utterances.speaker: ABDULLAH SALIHU [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, further north. Fairly nearby.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you able to see the effects of this bombing, what damage was caused to the town?

utterances.speaker: ABDULLAH SALIHU [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, because we were in a valley. We only saw the smoke rising when there was bombing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you travel near that area after you moved from the 29th of April?

utterances.speaker: ABDULLAH SALIHU [Resumed]
utterances.text: That time I was travelling in a truck, when we were taken from Fusha e Molles to the mosque and then from the mosque onwards.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. No further questions. Re-examined by Mr. Saxon:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Salihu, Mr. Kay asked you some questions about the 28th of April when NATO planes attacked the Ferronikel factory, and you made a comment that I'd like you to clarify, if you can. You mentioned that there were Serbs there - that's what you said - at that factory. What did you mean by that, that there were Serbs there?

utterances.speaker: ABDULLAH SALIHU [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were tanks, Serbian artillery, and the heaviest artillery that they had, which they kept in various places, at large buildings.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: These tanks and artillery were located at the Ferronikel factory that was bombed by NATO?

utterances.speaker: ABDULLAH SALIHU [Resumed]
utterances.text: When NATO bombed, I can't tell what there was inside, but certainly before the NATO bombing, there were tanks there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'd like to ask the assistance of the usher and of the Registrar if Exhibit 17, a photo collage, could be placed on the ELMO, please. I'd like to ask the witness a question about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While that's being done, Mr. Salihu, the accused asked you about the events of the 30th of April when you witnessed men being executed at Shavarina. You mentioned how three trucks came to the mosque, and the three trucks carried men to Shavarina, and over 30 men were taken off the truck --

utterances.speaker: ABDULLAH SALIHU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'd like, Mr. Usher, if you could place that photo collage on the ELMO so the witness can take a look at those photographs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Salihu, could you please take a look at the pages with photographs that are to your left. Take a look at the photographs themselves, Mr. Salihu. And if you could, please, tell us if you see on those photographs a vehicle that resembles the trucks on which the men were transported to Shavarina on that day. There's several pages there, so you may need to flip through the pages.

utterances.speaker: ABDULLAH SALIHU [Resumed]
utterances.text: This one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What number is that, Mr. Salihu? What number photograph?

utterances.speaker: ABDULLAH SALIHU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Number 8.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I have nothing further, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Salihu, that concludes your evidence. Thank you for coming to the International Tribunal to give it. You are free to go.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you for inviting me here to say what I went through myself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ryneveld.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. The next witness that we have scheduled is presently listed as Witness K4. I believe you have been advised by my colleague that this witness no longer seeks protective measures, and accordingly, will be proposing to give evidence live, as it were, without protective measures subject to, of course, our application before the court to have the evidence by way of 92 bis. Having said that, to this point, I'm not aware if the Court has had an opportunity to rule on our application to have his evidence go in the way of 92 bis, and so before I actually call him, I wonder whether perhaps that could be clarified.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Kay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. We received last night by fax a memorandum from the Registry, saying that this particular witness would be subject to attestation under the 92 bis procedure, and he is within the document filed by the Prosecution on the 2nd of May in which there's an attachment A, I believe Your Honours will be familiar with it, in which there is a large number of witnesses, the remaining witnesses within the Prosecution case, concerning this part of the joined indictment in which he features in that schedule as a witness that they would like to be included within the 92 bis procedure. The amici, at this moment, are still dealing with this motion as it involves a great deal of work for us to assess and evaluate the witnesses and make our own judgement about whether that would be appropriate or not in our view. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. I've been able to read the statement of this witness, K4. He is one of the insiders, a military man giving a great deal of detail, as he says, from what happened in Kosovo at this time as an insider within the military. It may well be that the Court has not had a chance to read his statement. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We have. We have.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Good.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: And it's true that there is detail. Most of it is related to one municipality and the activities there, and of course, one particular execution and massacre, it deals with that. It does deal with other matters.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: There is generality about the involvement of paramilitaries, the involvement of others within what took place in that particular region. If the Court permits the 92 bis procedure in relation to this witness, if I can put it that way, certainly there may well be a great deal of questioning from the accused which would exceed the normal hour with which he is allotted. One can see many issues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: That's something we would have to consider.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: But again, I raise this flag whether this Court would want this witness to go under the 92 bis procedure itself, because he is a witness of perhaps greater substance in relation to allegations within the indictment against the accused; whether that would be appropriate, we raise with the Court, because there would be concerns about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We will admit this witness's statement under Rule 92 bis since it is concerned with one municipality in the main. And although it is true it deals with some matters to do with the organisation of the VJ and the like, the evidence is cumulative in the sense that other witnesses give evidence about it, and it's cumulative in relation to Djakovica, the municipality involved. However, I think it right to say, Mr. Ryneveld, that we will look carefully, when it comes to these insider witnesses, as to whether Rule 92 bis is appropriate, and perhaps you would do the same. Perhaps you could reconsider the matter. I know there's a need for expedition, but we've got to balance the two.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Absolutely, Your Honour. You must appreciate that the Prosecution is prepared to proceed with live witnesses wherever necessary, but time constraints and expedition, we just propose, in order to attempt to meet the schedule, we must take whatever appropriate attempt that we can to put the evidence fairly before the Court in the most efficient manner, and for this witness, we felt that that was appropriate, to submit him for 92 bis. It may be that for the others, we will have to reconsider.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. The other point is that we will reconsider the time limits on the cross-examination, given the scope of the witness's statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Yes, and I may ask for the Court's indulgence with respect to this witness, for some indulgence on the five minutes that I need for preliminary questions, because some of the exhibits -- the Court may well benefit from a few questions about some of the exhibits that were attached to his statements in order to get some explanations as to how they came into being, because without a couple of words of explanation, that may be of some problem for the Court in understanding their significance.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: I'm only talking about the two maps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. Some explanation of the maps. The other point is we're not -- just one moment. We're not sitting -- we're not sitting in this case tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: No. I'm aware of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: So is the witness available for Monday, if need be?

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Yes, I believe so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I should like to draw your attention to the fact that this is not the first time that the other side over there holds a secret witness and then, on the day when that witness is to be examined, they explain that he is no longer a secret witness but a public witness. And everyone is aware of the fact how limited the possibilities are of amassing any kind of information about a secret witness. The same thing happened with the witness Veton Surroi, who was assigned a number K-something until the day he appeared to testify here and then he testified quite normally as a live witness and without any restrictions or limitations. Now we're faced with the same situation. As this is a repeat of the first situation -- that is to say, the first time, I thought it was just a mistake. Now as it's repeated itself, I don't think it is a mistake, I think it is ill-intentioned because it limits the possibility of collecting information about the secret witness, and then when he comes to be examined, he is proclaimed to be a public witness. At the same time, this witness is being introduced before the witness that was supposed to testify - Isuf Loku - and not him. So we thought that he would be -- it was stated that he would be on Thursday, and Thursday is a full working day. So why are we skipping a witness again? So once again, there is a change in the order of witnesses. I insist upon having a strict list and order for the witnesses at least for a week in advance and not to allow that order to be disturbed in any way and changed. If the other side is incapable of respecting the order and list of witnesses at least for a week, then it should be at its detriment and not at the detriment of the elementary functioning of even an illegal Tribunal of this nature.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We have dealt already with the Prosecution with the problems of the order of the list and required them where, unless it's absolutely essential, to stick to the list. Your allegation that there is ill-intention is one without substance. If we thought there was any question of motive or anything of that sort, we would not allow the Prosecution to do it. There is none. The witness has changed his mind about the protection, as I understand it. Mr. Ryneveld, is that the position?

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Absolutely, Your Honour. If I may just make a couple of comments about the allegation that's totally improper, the suggestion that the Prosecution is somehow making this witness public for some improper motive. The fact -- the fact is he's not been a secret witness to this accused. He's not been a secret witness to the amici. They have known his identity. The only issue was whether or not, when he testified, whether he would be testifying with a pseudonym and facial protection or not. This witness has indicated to the Prosecution that he now feels that he wants to testify openly. And in the interests of a public and transparent trial, we would encourage that wherever possible, and that is the reason and no other. But the accused has known this witness's identity, his real identity, it's not been secret to him. Secondly, we have also indicated that this particular witness will be been to testify on the 9th of May in the letters we have provided. We have always indicated that that was the date we intended to call the witness. If, because the scheduling and witnesses taking longer, we didn't get to Mr. Loku prior to today, that is a matter that's totally out of our hands, but we've always indicated that Witness K4 would be testifying today. And so with respect, the allegations are -- have no basis in fact.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: It's now --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just one question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: No. The matter is now concluded. It is now time for the adjournment. We will adjourn for 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. Let the witness take the declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. If you'd like to take a seat.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Examined by Mr. Ryneveld:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Peraj, would you give your full name to the Court, please.

utterances.speaker: NIKE PERAJ
utterances.text: My name is Nike Peraj.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Mr. Peraj, I understand, sir, that you are 55 years old, and you're a former teacher, and that you then became a captain in the Yugoslav army. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NIKE PERAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you remained a captain until sometime in June of 1999, just three days prior to NATO troops entering Kosovo; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NIKE PERAJ
utterances.text: Yes, a First Class Captain.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. And I understand, sir, that when you left the Yugoslav army, you were subsequently convicted in absentia by a military court for desertion; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NIKE PERAJ
utterances.text: Yes. That's what I've heard. But I have not received any document officially. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've heard that that's what happened, and you were tried and convicted and sentenced for desertion from the army?

utterances.speaker: NIKE PERAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand, sir, that your ethnicity is Albanian and that you are an ethnic Albanian, born in Kosovo; correct?

utterances.speaker: NIKE PERAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you belong to the Catholic faith. You're not Muslim.

utterances.speaker: NIKE PERAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I understand, sir, that you're married, with three children.

utterances.speaker: NIKE PERAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, did you give various statements to members of the Office of the Prosecutor of this Tribunal, the first of which was on the 18th of April of the year 2000? Did you provide a statement at that time?

utterances.speaker: NIKE PERAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And subsequently, did you provide a second statement in February of 2001, also to members of the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: NIKE PERAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And at that time, sir, did you provide some maps to attach as -- to attach to that second statement?

utterances.speaker: NIKE PERAJ
utterances.text: Yes, that's true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, I understand that subsequent to that, you arrived at the Tribunal and that yesterday, the 8th of May, you had an opportunity to review those statements in a language known to you and that you appeared before a presiding officer and made a solemn declaration that the statements you gave, as amended by you, were true to the best of your information and belief. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NIKE PERAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, at the time that you reviewed those statements, did you make some corrections to them before you gave your solemn declaration?

utterances.speaker: NIKE PERAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were those corrections recorded on -- on paper, and did you also solemnly declare that those corrections were true?

utterances.speaker: NIKE PERAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Your Honours, at this point I would like to tender a package, if I may, of the 92 bis procedure. And there are copies. Those passages would include all three, if I can call it that, statements, which included yesterday's corrections and the maps which are attached to the second statement. And I want to make this observation: That on the documents with the corrections yesterday, most of the cover pages, et cetera, all have the correct date, i.e., the 8th of May, 2002. However, the cover page of the corrections say the 18th of April. So that was just something that was missed off the cover page. That would be at ERN number that you have in the package, K0223426. That cover page has the date of the 18th of April because, when it was used as a precedent, they didn't change the date. But all other references show the 8th of May, 2002. Before I read the summary, I wonder whether -- I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Okay. Your Honours, that will be marked Prosecutor's Exhibit number 143.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. I would propose before reading a very brief summary of these statements, Your Honour, if this would be an appropriate time for me to ask the witness to clarify for the benefit of the Court these maps, just so that the Court can make some sense of them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Thank you. First I would ask that this large map be put on the ELMO, and perhaps Mr. Usher can assist. Unfortunately, Your Honours, the copy that I have has two colours on it, green and blue, but the copies that Your Honours would have are photocopies and, therefore, only show up in black. But there are three -- do we have three colour copies? We have the original and two copies in colour. Both the amici and the accused would have received these by disclosure a long time ago, with the appropriate colours, in the coloured version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. Let it be put on the ELMO and be given a separate exhibit number in a moment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Witness, first of all, I would like you to look at the map that is presently on the ELMO. First of all, do you recognise that document as a document that you made some notations on during the course of the taking of your second statement?

utterances.speaker: NIKE PERAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the colour that -- the map that you're looking at, does it have some markings in green pen and some markings in blue pen?

utterances.speaker: NIKE PERAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what were you attempting to describe in making these markings on this map? If we could start looking at the top of the map, if I can call it that, there is a marking --

utterances.speaker: NIKE PERAJ
utterances.text: The buildings marked and ringed in green are positions of places where the commands were stationed, garrison commanders, in Gjakove, and part of the command of the Pristina Corps at different times, also noted there. And in blue, I show where members of the police, i.e., police commands, were placed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So the green represents the VJ or the military, the army; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NIKE PERAJ
utterances.text: The army, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And blue signifies the MUP; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NIKE PERAJ
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, very briefly, sir, because time is of the essence and Their Honours will have had the benefit of reading your statement, perhaps you could simply outline for us, if we start at the top of the map at -- where I see at the end it's K2.4, do you know what that -- do you see the reference I'm making? Yes. Just put your pointer, so we're all clear what I'm talking about. No, to the right. To the right. Yes, right there. The green -- yes, right there. There are some things between two streets?

utterances.speaker: NIKE PERAJ
utterances.text: That was a private house, and in the cellar, the military police was stationed with soldiers and guards.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Then to your left, just moving down the map, if we can. At sort of the bottom of a curve, just to the left. Yes. What is that?

utterances.speaker: NIKE PERAJ
utterances.text: This was a building with -- also with a cellar where the command of the Gjakove brigade was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And there's both green and blue there. What does the green signify?

utterances.speaker: NIKE PERAJ
utterances.text: Green signifies the institute for social security in Gjakove, and this is where the police, the MUP, were sighted.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And there's also blue there in that location.

utterances.speaker: NIKE PERAJ
utterances.text: Green. And blue again. And this was part of the Pristina Corps, but the number 1 here shows that there was a police team here. There was part of the police here too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Perhaps you could indicate to us, just down below that, we see numbers where there is K2.3. What is that?

utterances.speaker: NIKE PERAJ
utterances.text: They stayed here two to three days.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I --

utterances.speaker: NIKE PERAJ
utterances.text: They stayed here two to three days, but I haven't noted here in which month.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. No, I'm just actually using the 2.3 as being a location. What was located there, sir, where you have the green circle? I'm just using those numbers to identify the location on the map for the record.

utterances.speaker: NIKE PERAJ
utterances.text: 2.3 was the command of the brigade here in Gjakove, in a private house, in the cellar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Sir, I'm going to try to speed this up a little bit by asking you, can you point out on this map for us the location of the Pristina Corps, if it is in fact on this map. The Pristina Corps garrison.

utterances.speaker: NIKE PERAJ
utterances.text: This was near the Lajci Cafe, on what was called Marsal Tito Street, now Mother Theresa Street. And in front of it there was an old barracks in -- here, in Gjakove.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And just for the record, you pointed to --

utterances.speaker: NIKE PERAJ
utterances.text: This is marked with Roman I, 2.5.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And just so that we're clear where you're pointing, you're now pointing off --

utterances.speaker: NIKE PERAJ
utterances.text: Was --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- to the left of the map, near the legend; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NIKE PERAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. You were earlier referring to a location where we see Roman numeral III under the letters "ARBR." What is that? Down.

utterances.speaker: NIKE PERAJ
utterances.text: Point III --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: NIKE PERAJ
utterances.text: Where the command went to take shelter. This was the command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And finally, can you indicate to us where the 52nd Rocket Artillery Brigade was located that's referred to in the statement?

utterances.speaker: NIKE PERAJ
utterances.text: The ARBR -- in all the places where there is ARBR are places where the anti-aircraft artillery had its command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: ARBR means the Rocket Artillery Brigade, that's the way to shorten that?

utterances.speaker: NIKE PERAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see. And finally, there is some blue at the bottom, right-hand corner of the map where it says "Mustafa Bakia" and there's the words "MUP." What is that big circle? What does that signify? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: NIKE PERAJ
utterances.text: From the MUP building, everybody moved over to the new part of the Mustafa Bakia school and also the old Mustafa Bakia school. There are two schools here, but the small blue circles here are all private houses where policemen lived.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. I want to move on to another map, if I may, now, and that is also --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Before you do, that should have an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. This will be marked Prosecutor's Exhibit number 143.1.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
